articles.title: J-K: Two grenades seized, man arrested during forest operation - Awaz The Voice
articles.content: In a joint operation with security forces, Baramulla Police apprehended a man and recovered two hand grenades from the Baderkoot forest area of Tangmarg in Jammu and Kashmir, police said on Thursday. The apprehended individual has been identified as Ghulam Jeelani Reshi, a resident of Baderkote, Tangmarg. The operation was conducted by Baramulla Police in coordination with CICT Ftr BSF (112/06 Bn), 2RR and CRPF 176 Bn during an Area Domination Patrol (ADP) in the forest area. According to the police, one hand grenade was recovered from the possession of the apprehended individual. Subsequently, acting on his disclosure, security forces recovered another concealed hand grenade from the forest. An FIR has been registered at Police Station Tangmarg, and further investigation is underway to ascertain the source of the recovered explosives, their intended use and possible links, as per the release. Baramulla Police reiterated its commitment to maintaining peace and security in the area and appreciated the coordinated efforts of all security forces involved in the operation. Further investigation is still underway. Meanwhile, in a separate incident in Kishtwar, the bullet-riddled bodies of two missing Special Police Officers (SPOs) were recovered from Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district early Thursday, a day after they went missing from the remote Dachhan belt. READ MORE : Assam’s Zainal Abdin made cane costumes for film ‘Ramayana’ The two SPOs, identified as Babi Chand (57) and Rashpal Kumar (45), were posted with the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the local police at Kiyar village in Dachhan. They had gone missing on Wednesday while travelling from their camp to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah. Officials said the bodies were recovered early Thursday. However, the service weapons of the slain personnel were not found, raising suspicions of a possible militant angle in the incident. articles.title: India's First 'Amrit Bharat 3.0' Train Departs From New Delhi To Patna Amidst The Echo Of ...
articles.content: New Delhi: To ensure the convenience and safe travel of passengers on the occasion of Chhath Puja, the grand festival of folk faith, Indian Railways has taken a historic initiative. India's first state-of-the-art 'Amrit Bharat 3.0' train was flagged off for Patna from the New Delhi Railway Station at midnight on November 11 as a Chhath Puja Special train. Passengers present at the station on this special occasion warmly welcomed this initiative by Indian Railways. articles.title: Union minister highlights India's rise as a leading maritime nation - The News Mill
articles.content: ANI Photo | Union minister highlights India’s rise as a leading maritime nation Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal emphasised the growth and modernisation of India’s maritime sector over the past 12 years under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, stating that improvements in infrastructure, digitisation and governance have strengthened the country’s position among the world’s leading maritime nations. Speaking in Visakhapatnam, Sonowal noted significant progress in the three sectors of ports, shipping and waterways since 2014, which has led to enhanced operational efficiency, increased cargo-handling capacity and improved services for vessel owners and cargo handlers. ADVERTISEMENT Stay connected Make The News Mill your preferred source See more TNM stories when you search for news on Google. Add TNM on Google “For 12 years, since 2014, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the port, shipping, and waterways—all three sectors, the performance is unique and we could have been able to create a lot of success stories,” the Union Minister said. He attributed the maritime sector’s improvements to modernisation and digitisation, explaining that major ports, as well as some operated by private entities and state governments, are now functioning more efficiently. ADVERTISEMENT “Because of the modernisation and digitisation, now all the major ports and also some of the ports in the private sector and the state government are running better, and because of the successful performance, we were able to increase our cargo handling capacity and also able to give service within a short span of time to the vessel owners and also the cargo handlers,” Sonowal stated. The minister highlighted India’s extensive coastline as a significant advantage for maritime development. “We have more than 11,093 kilometres of coastal areas, and that is the biggest advantage for us,” he said. ADVERTISEMENT He also credited the Centre’s policies and governance, along with the Prime Minister’s vision and efforts, for India’s growing stature in the global maritime domain. “Because of the Prime Minister’s strong vision, his untiring effort, effective policy and program and better governance, India is now standing as one of the leading maritime nations in the world,” Sonowal said. Earlier in Visakhapatnam, Sonowal inaugurated a waterfront promenade at Visakhapatnam Port and laid foundation stones for four new projects, with the total investment for the port’s new works reaching about Rs 560 crore. The Rs 19 crore Port Promenade stretches approximately 710 metres along the waterfront from the Venkateswara Temple to the International Cruise Terminal, covering about 5.5 acres. The promenade offers residents a regulated and safe area to observe ships and port operations for the first time. “It opens up the port to the city. This project is dedicated to the people of Visakhapatnam,” Sonowal said. The promenade features a waterfront walkway, two viewing decks including a Titanic-style viewpoint, a park, a public plaza, a children’s play area, a food court and visitor parking. articles.title: Hyderabad's Panjagutta to become India's first AI Police Station - ANI News
articles.content: Hyderabad (Telangana) [India], November 12 (ANI): Hyderabad City Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar said that Panjagutta Police Station is being developed as the country's first AI-based police station. He revealed that, as per the directions of DGP C.V. Anand, IPS, all services in this station are being integrated with state-of-the-art AI technology under a pilot project. On Wednesday, the CP conducted a surprise inspection of Panjagutta Police Station. On the occasion, he directly spoke to the complainants who came to the station and enquired about their problems. Later, he enquired in detail about the performance of each staff member in the station and the duties they were performing. He personally inspected the AI technology arrangements being made in the station, along with ACP Murali Krishna and Inspector Jahangir. He said that the AI police station will be launched as a pilot project in the first week of December by the DGP. He explained that after comprehensively examining the results here, this system will be implemented in all stations across the state. He explained that through the 'Sethu' kiosk already installed at the station reception, victims can lodge their complaints in nearly 10 languages, and AI technology will translate them into the local language and send them to the concerned officers within moments. He said that everything, from FIR registration to case diary, investigation reports, and charge sheet preparation, will be done using AI. City CP V.C. Sajjanar, IPS, said that by analysing details like congestion, hostels, commercial complexes, and crime history in the Panjagutta area, Blue Colts and the patrolling system will be run more efficiently, and special training is being given to staff on the use of technology. (ANI)

articles.title: Punjagutta PS to become India's 1st AI -powered station - The New Indian Express
articles.content: HYDERABAD: Punjagutta police station is set to become India’s first Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered police station, with AI technology being integrated into various stages of police functioning, from complaint registration to charge-sheet preparation. DGP CV Anand is scheduled to inaugurate the facility as a pilot project in December. On Wednesday, Hyderabad Police Commissioner Sajjanar inspected Punjagutta police station and said it was being developed into the country’s first AI-powered police station. Following the directives of DGP CV Anand, the station’s services are being integrated with AI technology as part of the pilot project. Under the initiative, AI will be used in processes ranging from the registration of First Information Reports (FIRs) to the preparation of case diaries, investigation reports and charge sheets. During the inspection, the Commissioner interacted with complainants and enquired about their grievances. He also reviewed the AI-based technical arrangements being put in place at the station. Sajjanar said a ‘SETUtu’ kiosk had already been installed at the station’s reception, enabling victims to lodge complaints in nearly 10 languages. The AI system translates the complaints into the local language and forwards them to the concerned officials. articles.title: Hyderabad: Panjagutta set to become India's first AI -powered police station - NewsMeter
articles.content: Hyderabad: Panjagutta police station is set to become India's first artificial intelligence (AI)-powered PS. Under the new project, the AI technology is being integrated into key policing functions, ranging from receiving public complaints and registering FIRs to preparing investigation reports and chargesheets. The initiative will be launched as a pilot project in the first week of December under the directions of Telangana Director General of Police (DGP) C.V. Anand, Hyderabad Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar said on Wednesday. The project aims to make police services more accessible, streamline investigations and improve operational efficiency through advanced technology. Complaints in 10 languages through AI One of the key features of the proposed AI-powered police station is a multilingual complaint registration facility. A 'Setu' kiosk, already installed at the police station's reception, allows complainants to submit their grievances in nearly 10 languages. AI technology will translate these complaints into the local language and instantly forward them to the concerned officers. The facility is expected to make it easier for people from different linguistic backgrounds to approach the police without facing language barriers. From FIR registration to chargesheet preparation AI technology will be integrated into several stages of police station operations, including: - Registration of First Information Reports (FIRs) - Preparation of case diaries - Drafting investigation reports - Preparation of chargesheets The move is aimed at reducing manual workload and helping police personnel handle documentation and investigation-related procedures more efficiently. AI to improve patrolling and crime prevention The Hyderabad Police will also use AI to analyse information about traffic congestion, hostels, commercial establishments and crime patterns within the Panjagutta police station limits. Based on these insights, the police plan to improve Blue Colts deployment and optimise patrolling operations. This is expected to help personnel identify vulnerable locations and strengthen preventive policing. Special training is being provided to police personnel to familiarise them with the new technology and its applications. DGP to launch pilot project in December Hyderabad Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar inspected Panjagutta Police Station on Wednesday to review the ongoing technological arrangements. During the surprise inspection, he interacted with complainants, enquired about their grievances, and reviewed the duties and performance of police personnel. He also examined the AI-related infrastructure along with ACP Murali Krishna and Inspector Jahangir. The AI-powered police station is scheduled to be inaugurated by DGP C.V. Anand in the first week of December as a pilot project. After assessing its performance, the Telangana Police plans to examine the possibility of implementing the model across police stations in the state, Sajjanar said.

articles.title: Niraj Kumar wins bronze at ISSF World Championship, secures India's first rifle quota for LA 2028
articles.content: ANI Photo | Niraj Kumar wins bronze at ISSF World Championship, secures India’s first rifle quota for LA 2028 Indian shooter Niraj Kumar won the bronze medal in the men’s 50m rifle 3 positions event at the ISSF World Championship in Doha on November 11. His third-place finish secured India’s first rifle quota spot for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Niraj scored 346.5 points in the final. Dmitrii Pimenov of Individual Neutral Athletes (AIN) claimed the gold medal with 362.8 points, setting a junior world record, while Slovakia’s Patrik Jany took silver with 357.2 points. ADVERTISEMENT Stay connected Make The News Mill your preferred source See more TNM stories when you search for news on Google. Add TNM on Google This medal marked India’s third consecutive podium finish in the men’s 50m rifle 3 positions event at the World Championships. Akhil Sheoran won bronze in 2023, and Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar secured silver in 2025. Tomar also competed in Wednesday’s final, finishing fifth with a score of 323.7. Niraj Kumar’s quota place brought India’s total Olympic quotas to two, following Jaypal Malviya’s silver medal performance in the men’s 10m air pistol event at the ISSF World Championships on November 10. Jaypal’s composed performance earned the country its first quota place for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics in that category. ADVERTISEMENT Jaypal scored 242.2 in the 24-shot final to take the silver medal. China’s Hu Kai won gold with 243.9 points, earning the first Olympic quota in the event. Czech Republic’s Jindrich Dubovy claimed the bronze medal and the third available quota place with 220.9 points. Jaypal remained in medal contention from the start, registering 50.5 in the first series and reaching 100.0 after the second. During the elimination stages, he maintained consistent high-10 scores, including 10.8 and 10.7, distancing himself from the competition. He held his composure in the final shots to retain second place behind Hu. Written by TNM (With ANI Inputs) This story is written by TNM Bureau with inputs from ANI. articles.title: Hyderabad AI Police Station Pilot to Launch in Panjagutta - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News Hyderabad’s AI Police Station Pilot Set to Launch in Panjagutta Breaking News Hyderabad’s AI Police Station Pilot Set to Launch in Panjagutta By Ayesha Siddiqui November 12, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Hyderabad’s Panjagutta police station is set to become India’s first AI-powered police station, with a pilot project planned for launch in the first week of December to support complaint registration, investigations and charge-sheet preparation. The initiative is being undertaken on the directions of Telangana Director General of Police C.V. Anand. Hyderabad Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar reviewed preparations during a surprise inspection of the station on Wednesday, where he interacted with complainants, examined their grievances and assessed the performance of police personnel. “From complaint registration to charge-sheet preparation, Artificial Intelligence will transform policing. A landmark step towards smarter, faster and more citizen-centric policing,” Sajjanar said. The proposed system will include an AI-enabled Setu kiosk through which complainants can submit grievances in about 10 languages. The system will translate complaints into the local language and forward them to the relevant authorities, according to the report. AI tools are also planned to support several internal policing functions, including First Information Report registration, case diary maintenance, investigation reports and charge-sheet preparation. The system is intended to connect the initial recording of a complaint with subsequent documentation in a case, although the supplied report does not specify the technology provider, procurement process or safeguards for handling personal data. During the inspection, Sajjanar was accompanied by Assistant Commissioner of Police Muralikrishna and Panjagutta police inspector Jahangir. He examined the AI-based systems being developed at the station and reviewed how the technology would be integrated into the station’s operations. The pilot will also use data relating to traffic congestion, hostels, commercial establishments and crime patterns in Panjagutta. Police said this analysis would help strengthen policing strategies, optimise the deployment of Blue Colts and improve patrolling efficiency. Blue Colts are police patrol units used in Hyderabad for local response and surveillance. The proposed deployment places the police station at the intersection of citizen-facing services and operational data. Complaint translation could reduce language barriers at the point of registration, while the planned use of area-level information is intended to help police allocate patrol resources. The report does not provide details on how residents will be informed about the system or how complaints requiring immediate intervention will be handled. Police personnel will receive special training to use the technology. The Panjagutta project is being treated as a pilot, and the model will be considered for implementation across Telangana based on its performance. The next stated milestone is the planned launch of the pilot in the first week of December. articles.content: Home Breaking News Hyderabad Police to Launch India’s First AI Police Station Breaking News Hyderabad Police to Launch India’s First AI Police Station By Ayesha Siddiqui November 12, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Hyderabad’s Panjagutta police station will be developed as India’s first AI-powered police station, with the pilot expected to launch in the first week of December under the directions of Telangana Director General of Police C.V. Anand. The initiative will use artificial intelligence across several stages of police work, including complaint registration, FIR registration, case diary maintenance, investigation reports and charge-sheet preparation. Hyderabad Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar reviewed the progress during a surprise inspection of the station on Wednesday. Sajjanar interacted with complainants, enquired about their grievances and reviewed the performance of police personnel during the visit. He was accompanied by ACP Muralikrishna and Panjagutta inspector Jahangir, and examined the AI-based systems being developed for the pilot. “From complaint registration to charge-sheet preparation, Artificial Intelligence will transform policing. A landmark step towards smarter, faster and more citizen-centric policing,” Sajjanar said. A key component of the system will be the AI-enabled Setu kiosk. According to the police, complainants will be able to submit grievances in about 10 languages through the kiosk. The system will automatically translate the complaints into the local language and forward them to the concerned authorities. The proposed station will also use data from Panjagutta to support policing decisions. Information relating to traffic congestion, hostels, commercial establishments and crime patterns in the area will be analysed to strengthen policing strategies, optimise the deployment of Blue Colts and improve patrolling efficiency. The pilot places Panjagutta at the intersection of several urban policing demands: a high-volume complaint system, multilingual access, traffic management, commercial-area surveillance and the deployment of mobile patrol units. The source report does not specify the artificial intelligence platforms, data protection safeguards, procurement cost or the process through which residents will be able to challenge an incorrect translation or AI-assisted record. Police personnel will receive special training to use the technology. The Telangana Police will assess the performance of the pilot before considering whether the AI police station model should be implemented at other locations across the state. The reported launch in December and the subsequent evaluation will determine the next stage of the programme.
